subject: Discovery Recap: Multi-tenancy controls (rate limits, routing, quotas)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Johnson <amelia@fintechco.com>, Kyle Ramirez <kyle@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery Recap: Multi-tenancy controls (rate limits, routing, quotas)

Hi Amelia / Kyle —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and next steps so we have alignment. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Pain points (what you told us):
- No per-tenant rate limiting today; spikes from a few customers are causing downstream latency and throttling across shared endpoints.
- Need per-customer quotas and per-customer routing policies to ensure higher-tier customers get dedicated capacity and different SLAs.
- Want predictable cost allocation and reporting by tenant for chargebacks.
- Concerned about isolation for compliance (audit logs, KMS, and key separation).

Current stack / constraints:
- Front-end proxy + in-house token router; we use AWS and currently run shared GPU endpoints.
- PCI-adjacent workflows; planning a compliance review mid-2026.

Success criteria (how you’ll measure an initial win):
1) Per-tenant rate limits implemented with no more than 100ms p95 added latency.
2) Ability to assign customers to routing tiers (standard, premium) with predictable tail latency differences.
3) Billing reports by tenant with token-level breakdown.

Proposed Redwood capabilities relevant to you:
- Per-tenant quotas and rate limits (configurable per-route and per-tenant).
- Policy-based routing: route high-tier customers to Dedicated pools or specific models/quantized variants.
- Token-level cost reporting in Console + exportable billing.
- Audit logs and KMS integration for Private deployments.

Action items / next steps:
- Redwood: send detailed controls doc + pricing matrix for Dedicated tiers (attached). Target: Ben by EOD tomorrow.
- FinTechCo: share current QPS per customer sample (small CSV) and top 10 heavy users. Target: Amelia by Friday (03/06).
- Schedule a short technical deep-dive with Marissa (solutions engineering) to validate routing policies and test a PoC. Suggested times: next Tues/Wed.

Attaching: redwood-multi-tenancy-controls.pdf (controls + config examples) and a sample template for tenant quota mapping.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

From: Amelia Johnson <amelia@fintechco.com>

Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 18:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Multi-tenancy controls (rate limits, routing, quotas)

Thanks Ben — this looks right and helpful. A couple clarifications: 

- Priority: per-tenant rate limits + routing tiers are the immediate priority. We can defer deeper audit/KMS discussions until after we validate routing behavior.
- SLA expectations: for premium customers we need p95 < 200ms and < 500ms p99. If Dedicated routing helps us meet that reliably, that's our preferred path.
- Security: we need to ensure logs are exportable to our SIEM (Splunk). The SOC2 artifacts you mentioned would be helpful.

I'll pull together the QPS sample and a list of top 10 tenants — aiming to share by Friday. Also happy to lock a time for the technical deep-dive; next Wed (03/10) in the morning PT works for our eng leads.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Amelia

amelia@fintechco.com
